evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-01"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-01". Creating a todo without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The value is a plain YYYY-MM-DD date, and a datetime string was rejected.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/4 with {"dueDate":"2026-09-01"} returned 200 with the new date. PATCH with {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null. A later GET /todos/2 after the same removal also showed null. PATCH with a new date set it again.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30", "23.10.2026", "2026-10-23T10:00:00Z", "abc" and the number 5 each returned 400 with 'dueDate must be a YYYY-MM-DD date or null'. PATCH with "2026-02-30" also returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Test data, with today 2026-10-23: past-due open todo, future-due todo, due-today todo, no-due todo, past-due todo marked done. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the past-due open todo (id 1, 2026-10-01). Future, today, no-due and done todos were excluded.
evidence.AC5: The page at / showed 'past fällig: 2026-10-01', 'future fällig: 2026-12-01', 'today fällig: 2026-10-23' and 'pastdone ✓ fällig: 2026-10-02'. The todo without a due date showed none.
evidence.AC6: In the page snapshot only the 'past' todo (open, due 2026-10-01) carried 'überfällig'. The future, due-today, no-due and done-past-due todos did not.
evidence.AC7: The page has a button 'nur überfällige'. Clicking it left only the 'past ... überfällig' item in the list. The other four items were hidden.
